item.name: Fhir
FHIR R4 CapabilityStatement — exactly what this gateway supports, nothing more.

request.name: FHIR R4 CapabilityStatement — exactly what this gateway supports, nothing more.

description.content: No bearer key required (this is the same discovery document for every caller); Content-Type is application/fhir+json, not the {data} envelope. Lists ONLY the resources/interactions this gateway actually serves — Patient, Appointment, DocumentReference (notes), Condition, AllergyIntolerance, MedicationStatement, MedicationRequest, Practitioner (providers), Coverage, Organization (insurance payers) and MedicationKnowledge (inventory items), search parameters limited to the query filters the plain JSON routes already accept. There is no _include/_revinclude and no general /fhir passthrough — see the developer guide (api-docs/fhir.mdx) for what a partner will not find.

response.name: OK.

item.name: Permanently delete an item that has never been used. Anything with history is refused — archive it instead.

request.name: Permanently delete an item that has never been used. Anything with history is refused — archive it instead.

description.content: Deleting is permanent and only possible for an item that has never been used: no stock, no stock history, and not part of any order, count, recipe or dispense. Anything else is refused with `item_has_history` (409) — archive the item instead; archiving is reversible and keeps the history. No Idempotency-Key is needed: sending the same delete twice returns `404` the second time.

item.name: Import up to 100 patients from a FHIR Bundle, NDJSON, or a JSON array. Nothing is written unless every row is valid.

request.name: Import up to 100 patients from a FHIR Bundle, NDJSON, or a JSON array. Nothing is written unless every row is valid.

description.content: The same import the app's Patients screen offers, for the clinic's OWN key. The file is checked in full before anything is written: every row goes through the same validation a real create does. If EVERY row is valid the import runs at once and the response is the finished job (`status: succeeded`). If ANY row fails, nothing is written and the response is the job with `status: needs_review` and a `row_errors` list — row number, field and reason for each, never the value that failed. Fix the file and send it again, or call `runValidPatientImportRows` to import only the rows that passed. A file with exactly the same content that has already been imported is refused `already_imported`, so retrying a timed-out call is safe; no Idempotency-Key is needed or read. An import contacts no patient and starts no automation. A possible duplicate is still created and counted in `flagged_duplicate`, for staff to review. Limits: 100 rows and 10 MiB, refused before any row is read. Needs `patients:write`, the API add-on and the accepted API data agreement. Only a clinic's own key may import — an organization connected to the clinic may not, whatever it was granted (`not_found`).

request.name: Reschedule or update an appointment. Immutable after create — patient_id, service_id, location_id, every payment field — are refused if sent.

description.content:
A new `start_at` or `clinician_id` is checked exactly as a new booking is (the slot must be free and the clinician bookable). Other fields are plain edits; an absent field is unchanged. `status` may only move to `confirmed` here; use the cancel route to cancel. A cancelled, completed or no-show appointment cannot be changed. With a test key the same edits work on the sandbox's fictional appointments, including a new time; a sandbox time is in UTC, and a slot that overlaps that clinician's other sandbox appointments is refused with `slot_taken`.

Who is told. For a live (non-test) appointment that is still booked and in the future, changing `start_at`, `clinician_id` or `venue_type` emails the patient and any participants: a new time is a reschedule notice, a new clinician or venue is an "Appointment updated" notice. The clinicians involved are told in the app and by email: the new clinician that a visit was added, the previous clinician that it was removed, or the current clinician that it moved. This follows the clinic's appointment notification setting and each clinician's own email setting. With `email_notifications` false on the appointment the patient is not emailed, but the clinicians still are. Each later change sends its own notice, and the patient's reminder is re-armed for the new time. Test-key appointments never send email.

request.name: List one patient's prescriptions (read only).

description.content: `patient_id` is required. Prescriptions are read only and minimal: the drug, the dose, the frequency, the status and when it was written, with `source` telling a prescription sent through the clinic's e-prescribing connection (`eprescribe`) from one written in the clinic (`clinic`). A prescription that exists only in the clinic's e-prescribing service is listed for the clinic's own keys only, never for an organization's key. There is no route to create or change a prescription. `status` filters by the prescription's status. A restricted patient's prescriptions, and any the clinic has marked sensitive, are never returned. With `Accept: application/fhir+json` the answer is a searchset Bundle of FHIR R4 MedicationRequest resources.

request.name: Submit a referral to the clinic for its staff to confirm.

description.content: The referral is held for review and answers 202 Accepted with a `Location` header pointing at the submission; it is not on the clinic's referral list until staff confirm it (unless the clinic has chosen to accept such submissions automatically). Confirming adds it as `received` - it does not accept the referral or book anything; the clinic decides that next, and a sender cannot. The `Idempotency-Key` header is REQUIRED - a retry with the same key returns the original submission, never a second one. This is a clinical referral, not the clinic referral programme. JSON only: a FHIR ServiceRequest body is not accepted.

item.name: Propose a change to a referral you sent, or retract it.

request.name: Propose a change to a referral you sent, or retract it.

description.content: The change is held for clinic staff to confirm and answers 202 Accepted with a `Location` header pointing at the new submission; the referral is unchanged until then. You can change a referral only while the clinic has not acted on it (`status: received`); after staff accept, decline, schedule, complete or cancel it, the request is refused with a 400 saying the clinic has already actioned it. `status: entered_in_error` proposes a retraction, also only while `received`. A sender cannot accept, decline, schedule, complete or cancel a referral. The service cannot be changed. The `Idempotency-Key` header is optional. JSON only: a FHIR ServiceRequest body is not accepted.

header.description: Optional. A unique value you choose for this request, such as a UUID. When sent, a retry with the same key returns the first answer instead of applying the change twice. See Retries and idempotency.

item.name: Providers
List the clinic's providers (its clinicians).

request.name: List the clinic's providers (its clinicians).

description.content: The clinic's directory of clinicians: the staff who can author clinical notes, excluding expired memberships. It is read only — there is no way to create, change or remove a provider through the API. Each provider carries the name, title, role, specialties, department, NPI and licences the clinic holds for them; email, phone and every other staff detail are never exposed, and there is no verified flag. `q` (at least 2 characters) matches the provider's name. The provider `id` is the same id the clinician pickers use. With `Accept: application/fhir+json` the answer is a searchset Bundle of FHIR R4 Practitioner resources.

request.name: Open a visit as a draft note.

description.content: Opens a visit for a patient as a DRAFT note a clinician completes, and answers 201 Created with the encounter (`status: draft`, `review_status: pending`). Nothing is ordered, prescribed, signed, locked or billed, and no note text can be sent; the draft appears in the clinic's consultation list for a clinician to finish. A restricted patient is a 404. The `Idempotency-Key` header is REQUIRED — a retry with the same key returns the original encounter, never a second draft. Send JSON; a FHIR Encounter body is refused.

description.content: Server-to-server REST API over a clinic's own non-PHI inventory data, reached with a clinic-owned key. No PHI scope exists yet — every operation below carries x-phi: false. A workspace's TEST key resolves ONLY to that workspace's own synthetic sandbox clinic, never a real one; `sandbox: true` on `Me` and on a `GET /v1/connections` entry marks that the data behind it is the seeded sandbox, not a real clinic's catalogue. The five inventory operations below are unchanged in their request/response shape for a sandbox call — the database, not this document or the router, decides which store answers. Every list operation (`GET …/inventory/locations`, `GET …/items`, `GET …/stock`, `GET /v1/connections`) wraps its rows as `{ data, has_more, next_cursor }`. `POST …/inventory/availability` wraps its rows as `{ data }` only (no pagination — it answers exactly the entries it was asked about). This is the gateway's actual, deployed behaviour; `_shared/ehr-api/openapi/response-envelope-parity.test.ts` pins it.
